subject: physics
title: Magnets and magnetic materials
key_idea: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract. Iron, steel, cobalt and nickel are magnetic materials. A permanent magnet has its own magnetic field. An induced magnet is only magnetic while it is in a magnetic field.

sections.heading: Poles and the forces between magnets

blocks.text: A magnet has two poles, where the magnetic forces are strongest. Two magnets exert forces on each other when they are close together.

items.meaning: The place on a magnet where the magnetic forces are strongest.
A force that acts without the objects touching.

items: Two like poles repel each other.
Two unlike poles attract each other.
Attraction and repulsion between magnetic poles are non-contact forces.
To show both forces, bring two unlike poles together, then two like poles together.

blocks.text: A magnetic fastener, such as the magnets in a coat, needs unlike poles facing each other. Two like poles would repel and the coat would not fasten.

items: Like poles repel. Unlike poles attract.

blocks.text: Only a few materials are magnetic. A magnet attracts a magnetic material.

items: Iron, steel, cobalt and nickel are magnetic materials.
Aluminium, copper, gold and zinc are not magnetic.
A magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans. Steel is magnetic and aluminium is not.

blocks.text: Some of these materials keep their magnetism and some do not. Permanent magnets keep it. A temporary magnet, such as the iron core of an electromagnet, can be switched on and off.

diagram.alt: Sort materials into those a magnet attracts and those it does not.
diagram.prompt: Is the material attracted to a magnet?

items: Iron, steel, cobalt and nickel are magnetic materials.
A magnet attracts them. It has no effect on non-magnetic metals such as aluminium.

blocks.text: There are two kinds of magnet. They differ in whether the magnetism stays when a magnet is taken away.

items.meaning: Produces its own magnetic field, all the time.
A material that becomes a magnet when placed in a magnetic field. It loses most or all of its magnetism quickly when removed.

diagram.alt: Permanent magnets compared with induced magnets.

values: Only while in a magnetic field

rows.feature: When a magnet is taken away
values: Loses most or all of its magnetism quickly

items: Induced magnetism always causes a force of attraction.
Only a permanent magnet can be repelled by another permanent magnet.
To test an iron bar, bring one end near each pole of a permanent magnet. Any repulsion shows it is a permanent magnet.
To show induced magnetism, use a magnet to pick up a paper clip, then remove the magnet. The clip no longer attracts other clips.
A permanent magnet has its own field. An induced magnet only has one while in a field.
Only repulsion proves an object is a permanent magnet.

checks.q: Which two of these are magnetic materials: cobalt, copper, gold, steel, zinc?
Describe how a permanent magnet could be used to test whether an iron bar is also a permanent magnet.
checks.a: Bring the same end of the iron bar close to each pole of the permanent magnet. Any repulsion shows the iron bar is a permanent magnet.

checks.q: State what is meant by an induced magnet.
checks.a: A material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field. It loses most or all of its magnetism when removed from the field.

exam_phrases: bring two unlike poles close together
bring two like poles close together
the paperclip would still be attracted to the magnet
any repulsion shows the iron bar is a permanent magnet

mistakes.wrong: Attraction shows that an iron bar is a permanent magnet.
mistakes.right: Only repulsion shows a permanent magnet. If one end is attracted to both poles it is not a permanent magnet.

mistakes.wrong: The iron rods move apart because they become charged.
mistakes.right: They become (induced) magnets, temporarily magnetised, with the same polarity at each end. Saying they become charged is not accepted.

mistakes.wrong: A paper clip would not be attracted to the south pole because it is not a magnet.
mistakes.right: It would still be attracted, because of induced magnetism. The paper clip becomes an induced (temporary) magnet.

worked_example.question:
A magnet produces a magnetic field. There are three metal blocks that are not labelled. One block is a permanent magnet, one is iron and one is aluminium.

Describe how another permanent magnet can be used to identify the blocks.
answer_points: The permanent magnet has no effect on the aluminium.
Iron is attracted to the permanent magnet.
Only the (permanent) magnet can be repelled by the permanent magnet.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each block identified correctly.

exam_phrases: remove the magnet (from the paper clips)
paperclips no longer attracted to each other
would be magnetised (when switch is closed)
would be demagnetised when switch is open

mistakes.wrong: All metals are attracted to a magnet, so the cans stick to the roller.
mistakes.right: Steel is a magnetic material and aluminium is a non-magnetic material. Only the steel cans are attracted.

mistakes.wrong: To test whether paper clips kept any magnetism, see if a magnet attracts them.
mistakes.right: A magnet attracts any magnetic material, so this is not accepted. Use a plotting compass, or bring the clips together and look for attraction or repulsion.

mistakes.wrong: An iron rod is used in the demonstration because it is a permanent magnet.
mistakes.right: Iron is magnetised when the switch is closed and demagnetised when it is open. It is not a permanent magnet.

worked_example.question:
A student has a bar magnet, a piece of iron the same size as the magnet, and some paper clips.

Describe how the student could use these items to demonstrate temporary induced magnetism.
answer_points: Place the iron near or in contact with the magnet, so it becomes a temporary magnet (or use the magnet to pick up a paper clip).
Show that the iron has magnetic properties: paper clips are attracted to it (or the first paper clip picks up another).
Show the effect is temporary: remove the magnet and the paper clips are no longer attracted, or they fall off.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for producing the induced magnetism, showing its magnetic properties, and showing the effect is temporary.

exam_phrases: Induced magnets lose their magnetism (when away from a magnetic field)
Permanent magnets retain their magnetism (when away from a magnetic field)
A temporary magnet which is only magnetic when it is within a magnetic field
the opposite pole has been induced at the top of the paperclip

mistakes.wrong: An induced magnet is a permanent magnet which is always magnetic.
mistakes.right: An induced magnet is a temporary magnet which is only magnetic when it is within a magnetic field.

mistakes.wrong: A magnet picks up a paper clip because the same pole is induced at the top of the clip.
mistakes.right: The opposite pole is induced at the top of the paper clip, so the two attract.

worked_example.question: Describe one difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet.
answer_points: Induced magnets lose their magnetism when away from a magnetic field.
OR permanent magnets retain their magnetism when away from a magnetic field.
worked_example.tip: Any one of the two points scores the mark.
